name: Liverpool 2018/19
scopeNote: Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp, 2018/19: 97 PL points (2nd), Champions League winners (2-0 v Tottenham, 1 June 2019). Period = first competitive match (PL v West Ham, 12 Aug 2018; pre-season friendlies excluded) to the final. Style term used by sources: gegenpressing / counter-pressing, 'organised chaos' (Melwood term, Goal Feb 2019); 'heavy metal football' is Klopp's own phrase vs Wenger's possession football (c.2013). Season-specific features: Fabinho and Keita signed, 4-3-3 with a switch to 4-2-3-1 (Firmino roving No.10, Salah No.9, Shaqiri on the right) in autumn/winter 2018, abandoned in winter; Alisson as sweeper-keeper and long passer; more controlled, less vertical than 2017/18 per Alisson. Coaches' Voice is a 2024 retrospective but states 2018/19 facts. Set-piece defending marking system for 2018/19 not verified from a reliable source (only an FM Scout blog describing a zonal/man hybrid); PPDA figures not verified from an accessible page.
openQuestions: Marking at defensive corners in 2018/19: only an FM Scout blog (tier D) describes a zonal + man hybrid with three zonal at the six-yard box, two post men, four man-markers and one outlet; Klopp's own quote (Monday Night Football 2016/17) says he moved away from Dortmund man-marking. No tier A-C 2018/19 source found.
PPDA: Tifo/This Is Anfield summary gives 8.05 (16/17), 9.45 (17/18), 10.08 (18/19) but the page was 403; Premier League site gives 11.2 for 2017/18 (different definition). Do not mix definitions.

Heavy-metal link: Goal (2021) ties 'heavy metal football' to gegenpress, high line, front three and attacking full-backs and cites 2018/19 points record; but 2018/19 sources (Premier League Nov 2018, Alisson in SI, Tifo) describe a less relentless, more controlled press than 2016-18. Candidate team link for heavy-metal-football is therefore weaker than 2016/17 or 2017/18 on pressing; stronger on front three, full-back width and transitions.

Distinctness from 2021/22: 2018/19 had a 4-3-3 with Fabinho/Henderson/Wijnaldum, a stretch of 4-2-3-1, Alisson long passing, no Diogo Jota/Thiago; 60% possession or more (Coaches' Voice). Build-up detail (long balls to the front three) is thin: only Alisson's 172 accurate long passes and 'back to front incisiveness'.
Alexander-Arnold inverting to midfield and 3-2 build-up in Coaches' Voice belongs to 2022-24, not 2018/19; not recorded.
Several Coaches' Voice facts come from a 2024 retrospective; set-pieces line about full-backs' deliveries is not dated precisely to 2018/19.
Squad age: only FourFourTwo's 'just reaching or not yet at their prime'; no exact average age found.
Pressure/PPDA and corner-taker data (Alexander-Arnold corners) not found beyond the Barcelona quick corner and Coaches' Voice line.
